en.headline: Po Leung Kuk scraps student eco-bag contest after outcry
en.dek: The charity cancelled its “From Martial Love to Love” design competition for primary pupils after public criticism that the theme risked normalising domestic violence.
body: Po Leung Kuk has cancelled a primary-school eco-bag design competition after the promotional material drew strong public criticism. The contest, titled “From Martial Love to Love”, had invited pupils to create designs based on seven common household items described as “weapons of love”.

The listed items included an umbrella, belt, folding stool, knife, insecticide, wine bottle and clothes hanger. Accompanying slogans urged participants to transform the objects into positive expressions of affection. The poster circulated widely on social media and prompted accusations that the framing risked trivialising or aestheticising domestic violence.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the charity said the form of expression had caused public concern and misunderstanding. After internal review it decided to cancel the activity and remove related posts. Po Leung Kuk reaffirmed its firm opposition to domestic violence and said it would draw lessons for future programmes. The event had been organised by its family crisis support service with Social Welfare Department funding.

zh.headline: 保良局取消「從武愛到有愛」環保袋比賽
zh.dek: 活動宣傳以「七大家暴武器」為題引發網民批評美化家暴，保良局周四宣布取消比賽並刪除相關帖文。
body: 保良局已取消一項小學環保袋設計比賽。比賽原名「從武愛到有愛」，要求學生以雨傘、皮帶、摺凳、刀、殺蟲水、酒樽及衣架等七項物品為主題創作，宣傳標語呼籲將這些「愛的武器」轉化為正面表達。
宣傳海報在社交平台廣泛流傳後，不少網民批評活動有美化或輕視家暴之嫌。保良局周四回應指，活動表達形式引起公眾疑慮及誤會，經檢討後決定取消活動，並已刪除相關宣傳帖文。
保良局重申堅定反對家庭暴力，並關注家暴對兒童的影響，表示會汲取經驗，日後以更合適方式推行相關活動。該比賽由保良局家庭危機支援服務主辦，獲社會福利署資助。
